findings.evidence: Previous-version digest at dbff837f: 'removed units (479, showing 40)'. All 40 units shown are explained, either by valid rows in docs/audit/recovery/design-system-starter/record.md through sections.json, or by restored content in references/token-scales.md, references/component-examples.md and references/process-and-tooling.md. The other 439 units could not be checked one by one.
findings.fix: Re-run the removal check with the full unit list, or confirm that every unit not shown maps through sections.json to a record row whose (fate, value, decision) combination fixer-rules.md allows. Restore any unit without a row into references/, or add a row for it to docs/audit/recovery/design-system-starter/record.md.

findings.evidence: Body is about 70 lines of workflow and gotchas. A few step clauses restate habits the model already has ('Revise the API before wider adoption if consumers need repeated workarounds'), so not every line is expert-only.
findings.fix: Shorten that clause to the non-obvious part, the trigger 'repeated consumer workarounds'. Keep the other text, which is expert content.

findings.evidence: '## Resources' repeats, file by file, the loading triggers already written inline in workflow steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8. This is a small deviation from a lean Process pattern.
findings.fix: Turn the Resources list into a one-line index of each file's purpose with its step number ('token-scales.md: step 3'), and let the inline step triggers carry the conditions. Remove nothing: every file and every condition stays in the step that loads it.

findings.evidence: Eval 'accessible-dark-tokens' lists "files": ["templates/design-tokens-template.json", "templates/component-template.tsx", "references/component-examples.md"]. These are the skill's own bundled files, not eval inputs under evals/files/, so the with-skill and without-skill runs differ in more than the skill. trigger-queries.json also has 11 should-not-trigger queries, above the 8-10 target, and two are no-overlap negatives ('Convert our SVG icons...', 'Build a landing page...').
findings.fix: Remove the skill files from that eval's 'files' (the prompt has no user input files), or replace them with a real input under evals/files/, such as a small existing dashboard stylesheet. In trigger-queries.json, replace the SVG-icon negative with a near-miss that shares vocabulary, for example 'Generate a Figma variables export from our finished tokens.json'.

findings.evidence: 'Style Dictionary reads object colors from 5.3 and object dimensions from 5.4'. These minimum versions are version-sensitive vendor facts, and they have no source URL or date checked where they appear (README lists only the repository under Sources).
findings.fix: Add the Style Dictionary release notes or DTCG support doc URL and the date checked after the sentence, or replace the hard versions with an instruction to read them live: 'check the installed Style Dictionary changelog for DTCG 2025.10 object-value support before claiming 2025.10'.

findings.evidence: The template defines "intent?: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'danger'" and "size?: 'sm' | 'md'". The references/component-specs.md Button row specifies 'intent: primary, secondary, outline, ghost, danger; size: sm, md, lg' and a 'fullWidth' prop. An agent scaffolding from both gets two different Button contracts.
findings.fix: Make the two agree. Either extend the template's unions to the spec's (adding outline, ghost, lg and fullWidth?: boolean with documented defaults), or add one line to the component-specs Button row: 'the template ships the minimal primary/secondary/danger, sm/md subset; add the other variants additively with defaults unchanged'.

findings.evidence: Cut list (showing 40 of 218 removed units) from the dbff837f digest is one medium finding. The 40 shown units map to section ids s001-s054, each with an allowed record row. The second digest (89cb6a11) has 0 removed units.
findings.fix: No restore: the shown units are explained. Record the 178 unshown units in docs/audit/recovery/gemini/record.md only if a later digest shows one is substantive and unexplained.

findings.evidence: Workflow is a numbered procedure without a checklist, and step 6 leaves resume versus a new headless run as two open paths.
findings.fix: Add a short progress checklist to Workflow (scope, secret scan, run or propose, exit code, verify, follow-up) and make the headless follow-up the default: new -p run with accepted findings in the prompt, interactive --resume only when the user will run it in their terminal.

findings.evidence: Gotchas covers shell escaping the include list, positional prompts, timeout process groups, plan-to-yolo, silent tool denial, trust loading settings, and pkill, but not the 5-directory cap or a positional prompt combined with -p.
findings.fix: Add two Gotchas: a sixth --include-directories path is dropped (cap 5, configuration.md), and a positional argument next to -p is not the prompt and can open a session; put extra instruction only inside -p or on stdin.

findings.evidence: references/model-selection.md and references/troubleshooting.md are gated, but the sources list at lines 81-84 is ungated detail the agent does not need on every run.
findings.fix: Move the four source URLs and the 2026-11-07 check date into references/troubleshooting.md (or a references/sources.md) and leave one line in Gotchas: re-read that file or run gemini --help when a claim fails.

findings.evidence: Model choice is a default plus a reference menu, but step 6 offers interactive --resume and a new headless run as equal follow-ups, and yolo's sandbox requirement is only inside a table cell.
findings.fix: State one follow-up default in step 6 (new headless -p run; interactive --resume only when the user will run it). In Defaults, say yolo without a confirmed -s sandbox or an isolated copy is not allowed.

findings.evidence: Nine evals have realistic prompts and verifiable assertions, but none exercises the secret-file scan before launch or the 900s budget for a >200k-token or three-directory scope. Trigger queries are 10/10 with near-misses, yet several should-trigger lines are keyword-explicit.
findings.fix: Add one eval whose scope contains a .env or *.pem and asserts the command is not launched until the user decides, and one three-directory or >200k eval that asserts timeout 900. Rewrite two should-trigger queries so they omit the words Gemini and CLI.

findings.evidence: Step 4 says 124 means timeout (137 if KILL was needed) and maps only 0, 1, 42 and 53. The launch example uses timeout, so a killed run exits 137 from timeout, which the agent would treat as incomplete for the wrong reason.
findings.fix: In step 4, say a timeout-wrapped run returns 124 on TERM and 137 when KILL was needed; both mean the review is incomplete. Keep 1, 42 and 53 as Gemini's own codes when gemini itself exits.

findings.evidence: previous-version digest: gemini at dbff837f — removed units (218, showing 40)
findings.fix: The digest is cut off, so only 40 of the 218 removed units could be checked. Every unit shown maps to a valid section row in record.md (for example s023, s035, s042, s047 and s054 through sections.json). Re-run the judge with the full digest, or confirm that sections.json covers all 218 units, so the 178 unseen units can be checked against record.md.

findings.evidence: Description promises "big-context (>200k token) analysis of repositories, multi-directory projects or document sets", but Command shapes gives only code, plan and interactive commands, and the prompt criteria are left as "<criteria>"
findings.fix: Add one more Command shape for a doc set, for example cd into docs/ with --include-directories specs and -p "Find contradictions between these documents; cite file:section for both sides". Also add one line on how to split a scope over about 200k tokens into per-area runs before merging the verified findings.

findings.evidence: Several queries are terse and name the skill outright, with no realistic context: "use Gemini CLI for a cross-directory architecture review", "run a background Gemini review of the auth changes". Some negatives are easy, for example "summarize this one short source file".
findings.fix: Rewrite 3-4 positive queries to describe the need with file paths and personal context but without naming Gemini, for example "my manager wants a second pair of eyes on ~/work/billing before the audit, it's way too big for one pass". Replace the easy negatives with near-misses such as "run gemini-cli's /init in this repo" or "review this diff yourself, no other model".

findings.evidence: "`124` timeout (`137` if KILL was needed), `1` API or auth error, `42` bad arguments, `53` turn limit" — the Gemini CLI exit codes have no source URL or checked date. The Sources list below Gotchas covers only the policy engine, plan mode, trusted folders and include-directories.
findings.fix: Add a Sources line for the exit codes, for example "Exit codes 1/42/53: `cli/headless.md`, checked <date>". Or tell the agent to check `gemini --help` or the headless docs when it sees an unmapped code.

findings.evidence: Model table (gemini-3-pro-preview, gemini-3.1-pro-preview "rolling out", gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-2.5-* and aliases) has no source URL and no checked date
findings.fix: Add under the table: "Source: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/cli/model.md, checked <date>; `/model` in the CLI lists what the account can use." The model.md row already exists in docs/audit/upstream-sources.json.

findings.evidence: "`-y`/`--yolo` is deprecated; write `--approval-mode yolo`." This is a vendor CLI flag fact, it is not in the Sources list and has no checked date.
findings.fix: Add a Sources entry for the deprecation, for example "`-y` deprecation: `cli/cli-reference.md`, checked <date>", next to the existing Sources lines below Gotchas.

findings.evidence: 4d. Over the limit and the essential content cannot fit: ask whether to make a thread
findings.fix: Define essential before the length check: a fact or qualifier from the step 1 list that cannot be dropped. Move the definition next to step 4d; do not delete the length rules.

findings.evidence: 3c. Sensitive posts (grief, apology, factual updates): replace (b) and (c) with quieter variants
findings.fix: In step 3c name what a factual update is (a correction, outage or incident notice, or a post whose harm comes from spin) so a routine launch is not forced onto the quiet path. Keep the grief and apology cases.

findings.evidence: Unicode bold/italic "fancy text" costs 2 per glyph and screen readers read noise: never use it.
findings.fix: In Gotchas, say the 2-weight applies to the Unicode mathematical alphanumeric symbols people paste as bold or italic, not to markdown *emphasis*, which is not posted.

findings.evidence: 2. Pick the payoff and objective. Name what the reader gets (lesson, laugh, validation, news, or awe or surprise ... ) and choose one primary objective
findings.fix: When the supplied facts support more than one payoff, default to the payoff that matches the chosen objective (reposts: quotable news or validation; replies: a lesson the question tests; dwell: the complete observation) and name the rejected alternative in ANALYSIS.

findings.evidence: on yes, or if you cannot ask, VERSION 1-3 become three alternative threads ... In the three-thread case each VERSION block holds its thread ... omit THREAD
findings.fix: State one rule: when the user already said yes to a thread, or the run cannot ask, put each alternative thread in its VERSION block with posts numbered 1/n and per-post counts, and omit THREAD. Reserve THREAD for a single-post run the user has not yet answered about, and say that case still returns no over-limit standalone post.

findings.evidence: "The output asks the user to confirm or supply specifics (what the product is, a real number) instead of inventing them"
findings.fix: Rewrite the launch-idea prompt so it does not forbid asking while asserting that the output asks the user to confirm missing facts; keep the assertions that no rewrite invents a number, customer or dramatic event.

findings.evidence: Digest at dbff837f: 'removed units (75, showing 40)'. This is a cut list. Every unit does map to a section row in docs/audit/recovery/viral-tweet/sections.json (s001-s013), and each of those rows has an allowed (fate, value, decision) combination. The restored levers (closed curiosity gap, awe/surprise/validation payoff, ranked-list reply lever, sharing test, voice rules) are present in steps 2, 3a and 3d.
findings.fix: Regenerate the digest without truncation so all 75 units are listed and can be checked one by one. No content needs restoring: every unit is covered by a valid row in docs/audit/recovery/viral-tweet/record.md.

findings.evidence: Step 5 repeats the lever tests from step 3a almost word for word: 'replies needs one specific question the author wants answered, or a ranked or listed claim built only from supplied facts or the author's stated opinion; reposts needs ... passes the sharing test (the reader would look smart, informed or funny reposting it)'
findings.fix: In step 5, refer to the tests instead of restating them ('check the candidate against its step 3a lever test; dwell needs a concrete observation and a complete payoff; clarity needs the least ambiguity and emotional spin'). Keep the full wording in step 3a. No rule is lost.

findings.evidence: 'Add hashtag stacks, "link in bio", or unrelated @mentions or links.' This is the only NEVER item with no reason given.
findings.fix: Add the reason readers react to, for example: 'Add hashtag stacks, "link in bio", or unrelated @mentions or links: they read as spam and as marketing, so readers scroll past or mute.' Keep the link-substantiation rule.

findings.evidence: '**THREAD (only when a single-post run becomes a thread):**' The THREAD block has no branch that produces it. Step 4d says that on a yes, or when you cannot ask, 'VERSION 1-3 become three alternative threads', and line 53 says to 'omit THREAD' in that case.
findings.fix: Choose one path. Either delete the THREAD line and say that thread output always lives inside the VERSION blocks. Or define the case that uses it in step 4d (for example: 'if the user wants only the recommended single post expanded, output one THREAD and keep VERSION 1-3 as single posts').

findings.evidence: 'Estimate the weighted count against the 280 limit of standard X posts'. X sets this limit and has changed it before. The line gives no source URL and no date checked, and nothing tells the agent to read it live.
findings.fix: Add the official source and the date checked, for example '(X counting rules: https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/counting-characters, checked YYYY-MM-DD)'. Or tell the agent to confirm the limit in X's composer every time, not only within 15 characters of it.

findings.evidence: 'each URL or bare domain such as example.com/x counts 23'. The t.co link weight is a value X sets, and the line gives no source or date.
findings.fix: Cite X's official counting-characters documentation (or the twitter-text config) with the date checked, next to the 23-character URL weight.

findings.evidence: 'each CJK character and emoji 2'. The weighting ranges are a value X sets, and the line gives no source or date.
findings.fix: Cite the same official X counting documentation, with the date checked, for the weight-2 ranges (CJK, emoji). Keep the existing caveat that this is an estimate.
